# Security

Security is built-in, not bolted-on. Every feature, endpoint, and data flow must consider security implications.

## OWASP Top 10 (2025)

| #   | Vulnerability                      | Prevention                                      |
| --- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Broken Access Control              | Verify permissions server-side, default deny    |
| 2   | Security Misconfiguration          | Secure defaults, remove unused features         |
| 3   | Software Supply Chain Failures     | SBOM, dependency scanning, signed builds        |
| 4   | Cryptographic Failures             | Use TLS, hash passwords (argon2id), encrypt PII |
| 5   | Injection                          | Parameterized queries, input validation         |
| 6   | Insecure Design                    | Threat modeling, security requirements          |
| 7   | Authentication Failures            | Strong passwords, MFA, secure session mgmt      |
| 8   | Software or Data Integrity         | Verify dependencies, sign releases              |
| 9   | Logging and Alerting Failures      | Log security events, set up alerts              |
| 10  | Mishandling Exceptional Conditions | Fail securely, generic errors to clients        |

## Security Principles

| Principle          | Rule                                                      |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Defense in Depth   | Multiple layers: firewall, auth, authz, encryption, audit |
| Least Privilege    | Minimum permissions needed, nothing more                  |
| Zero Trust         | Never trust, always verify. Assume breach.                |
| Secure by Default  | HTTPS, strict passwords, secure cookies out of the box    |
| Fail Securely      | Access denied on error, no internal details to users      |
| Validate on Server | Client validation is UX, server validation is security    |

## Pre-Deployment Checklist

| Area          | Requirements                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Passwords     | Hashed with argon2id (preferred) or bcrypt (12+ rounds)             |
| Tokens        | JWT with EdDSA/ES256, 15min access / 7d refresh, httpOnly cookies   |
| Sessions      | HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookies                           |
| Rate Limiting | Auth endpoints: 5 attempts/15min                                    |
| Authorization | All routes check auth server-side, default deny                     |
| Input         | Validated with schema (Zod), parameterized SQL                      |
| Uploads       | Whitelist types, enforce size limits                                |
| Secrets       | No secrets in code or VCS                                           |
| Headers       | CSP (with nonces), HSTS, Permissions-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options |
| CORS          | Configured restrictively                                            |
| Encryption    | PII encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3)            |
| Logging       | Audit logging for security events                                   |
| Dependencies  | SBOM generated, `npm audit` clean, Dependabot enabled               |

## Threat Modeling (STRIDE)

| Threat                 | Category        | Key Mitigations                                        |
| ---------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Spoofing               | Authentication  | MFA, strong passwords, JWT with short expiry           |
| Tampering              | Integrity       | Input validation, HTTPS/TLS, signed tokens             |
| Repudiation            | Accountability  | Audit logging, digital signatures                      |
| Info Disclosure        | Confidentiality | Encryption, least privilege, secret management         |
| Denial of Service      | Availability    | Rate limiting, input validation, CDN/DDoS protection   |
| Elevation of Privilege | Authorization   | Authz checks on every request, ABAC, permission audits |

## Risk Levels

| Level    | Action                    |
| -------- | ------------------------- |
| Critical | Immediate action required |
| High     | Address before launch     |
| Medium   | Address post-launch       |
| Low      | Monitor, may accept risk  |

| PCI-DSS   | Credit card data   | Use payment processor (Stripe), tokenization, network segmentation |

## Anti-Patterns

# TypeSafe

> How to use TypeSafe's System One API

- [Introduction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction.md): Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first System One model. Send state and typed questions; get structured answers your code can use directly.
- [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md): Get up and running with Jev in 5 minutes.
- [Jev with coding agents](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/coding-agents.md): What Jev is (and isn't) when you're using a coding agent.
- [Example use cases](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/use-case-map.md): Explore TypeSafe use cases by industry and turn promising ideas into software workflows.
- [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md): System One models make fast, structured decisions for software. Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first System One model.
- [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md): What state is, how to structure it, and how to give a System One model the context it needs.
- [Primitives (Questions)](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives.md): The TypeSafe question types, the typed answers they return, how to choose between them, and how to ask several at once.
- [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md): A Choice is a System One question type for selecting one option from a defined set. The answer includes the selected option, a probability for each option, and confidence.
- [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score.md): A Score is a System One question type for rating content against ordered, descriptive levels. The answer includes a score, a probability for each level, and confidence.
- [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul.md): A Noul question asks the TypeSafe model to evaluate a yes/no question and return the probability that the answer is yes.
- [Box](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/box.md): A Box is a System One question type for finding where something is in an image. The answer is the four edges of a box around it, as fractions of the image's width and height.
- [Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced.md): Instructions, Choice options, Score levels, and Noul criteria all accept JSON structure.
- [Images](https://docs.typesafe.ai/images.md): Send images in a System One request: in the state, inside a question's instructions, and as the criteria a question is judged against.
- [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md): How TypeSafe reports certainty, how it differs from probability, and how to use it to control system behavior.
- [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md): Design AI-powered software by keeping code in control and giving System One narrow, structured decisions.
- [AI primer](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/machine-learning-primer.md): Why TypeSafe trains decision models with calibrated probabilities instead of optimizing for generated text.
- [Patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns.md): Architectural patterns for building systems with TypeSafe.
- [Speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md): Send many questions in a single call, including speculative ones, and let your code decide what's relevant.
- [Confidence-gated routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/confidence-routing.md): Use confidence as a second axis. The answer tells you what; confidence tells you whether to act.
- [Composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md): Break a complex judgment into atomic scores, combine with weights you control in code.
- [Intent routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/intent-routing.md): Classify incoming requests and route each to the optimal handler: deterministic logic, a specialist LLM, or a human.
- [Cookbooks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks.md): End-to-end recipes that show TypeSafe in real problems, from a few questions to full pipelines.
- [Function calling](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/function_calling.md): Turns natural-language trading requests into calls to ordinary typed functions by mapping function names and closed-set arguments to confidence-aware TypeSafe questions.
- [Skill suggestion](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/skill_suggestion.md): Picks at most one skill for an agent turn out of the 182 in Nous Research's Hermes catalog, using two TypeSafe requests to rank and re-check the top candidates.
- [Guardrails for LLMs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/llm_guardrails.md): Screen every message going into and out of an LLM app with one TypeSafe request, thresholding hazard probabilities and severity to pass, review, block, or route.
- [Double-checking citations](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/citation_check.md): Catch wrong or hallucinated citations by checking against the source document. One Choice question decides whether the quote's context supports the claim.
- [Classifying RAG passages](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/classifying_rag_passages.md): Score each retrieved passage with one TypeSafe request, then decide in code which ones reach the answering model.
- [Simple memory system](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/basic_memory.md): Let Jev decide which requests and answers are worth remembering, then wrap the Jev call in a small function that adds memories to later calls.
- [Hierarchical classification](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md): Classifies documents through deep patent, retail product, biomedical, and source-code hierarchies using parallel beam search over TypeSafe Choice probabilities.
- [Classification using confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/classification_using_confidence.md): Classify SEC annual reports into 75 industry groups with one Choice each, then read the answer's own confidence to decide whether to report that group or the broader division above it.
- [Twitch chat filter](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/twitch_chat_filter.md): Hide insults, spam, and unasked-for gameplay tips in Twitch chat, blur spoilers, and highlight questions. Each message gets one TypeSafe request containing multiple questions. Up to eight messages are processed concurrently, and the rules are defined in code.
- [SDE cascade](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/sde_cascade.md): Uses a 2-stage structured-data-extraction cascade (mini → verify → reasoning) to get most of the quality of a big reasoning model at a fraction of the cost.
- [Date extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/date_extraction_cookbook.md): Extracts absolute and relative dates by asking TypeSafe for the parts named in a document, then resolving and validating them in code with confidence-based review.
- [Pre-parsed value extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/pre_parsed_value_extraction_cookbook.md): Uses regexes to find candidate emails, phone numbers, and amounts, then has TypeSafe select the requested span so code can normalize a verbatim value.
- [Structure recovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoformat.md): Reconstructs Markdown from plain text that lost its formatting in two requests: one stitches hard-wrapped lines back together, one classifies every block (heading, list, code, callout).
- [Re-ranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md): Builds 30-passage BM25 shortlists for 40 CLERC legal queries, then uses one TypeSafe question per query-candidate pair to raise top-1 accuracy from 5% to 18% and top-10 accuracy from 38% to 62%.
- [Line-by-line search](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/semantic_find.md): Build semantic search for GitHub's Terms of Service. In one request, score 218 line ids against a plain-language query with a Choice question, and use a Noul question to check whether the document contains an answer.
- [Knowledge graph entity alignment](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/entity_alignment.md): Decides which of 450 candidate pairs from two beer catalogues describe the same product using one Score question plus three companion Nouls that surface which fields disagree.
- [Self-consistency: choices](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_choice_cookbook.md): Add an uncertain outcome to moderation decisions and compare label agreement with the share of automatic actions.
- [Self-consistency: nouls](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_noul_cookbook.md): Route uncertain probabilities to human review while keeping the underlying noul values visible.
- [Parallel questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/parallel_questions.md): Runs a 13-question regulatory briefing over the GDPR Wikipedia article, showing that batching every question into one TypeSafe call is 12.2x cheaper and 10.0x faster with no change in answers.
- [Autoresearch feature discovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md): Runs an autoresearch loop that proposes TypeSafe questions, converts free text into numeric features, and uses model errors to improve a supervised CatBoost regressor.
- [Demos](https://docs.typesafe.ai/demos.md): Interactive examples showing what's possible with TypeSafe.
- [Smart home assistant demo](https://docs.typesafe.ai/demos/smart-home.md): Demo code: a smart home assistant that uses TypeSafe to evaluate user requests.
- [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md)
- [Agent skill](https://docs.typesafe.ai/agent-skill.md): Drop-in skill for Claude Code, Codex, and other agent environments.
- [Legal](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal.md): Legal documents and policies for TypeSafe.
- [Jev 1.13 jaggedness](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md): Jev isn't perfect. Here are some jagged edges we are aware of with jev-1.13. Many of these will be fixed in later versions.
- [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/system-one.md): Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.

# TypeSafe

> How to use TypeSafe's System One API

- [Introduction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction.md): Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first System One model. Send state and typed questions; get structured answers your code can use directly.
- [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md): Get up and running with Jev in 5 minutes.
- [Jev with coding agents](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/coding-agents.md): What Jev is (and isn't) when you're using a coding agent.
- [Example use cases](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/use-case-map.md): Explore TypeSafe use cases by industry and turn promising ideas into software workflows.
- [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md): System One models make fast, structured decisions for software. Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first System One model.
- [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md): What state is, how to structure it, and how to give a System One model the context it needs.
- [Primitives (Questions)](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives.md): The TypeSafe question types, the typed answers they return, how to choose between them, and how to ask several at once.
- [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md): A Choice is a System One question type for selecting one option from a defined set. The answer includes the selected option, a probability for each option, and confidence.
- [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score.md): A Score is a System One question type for rating content against ordered, descriptive levels. The answer includes a score, a probability for each level, and confidence.
- [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul.md): A Noul question asks the TypeSafe model to evaluate a yes/no question and return the probability that the answer is yes.
- [Box](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/box.md): A Box is a System One question type for finding where something is in an image. The answer is the four edges of a box around it, as fractions of the image's width and height.
- [Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced.md): Instructions, Choice options, Score levels, and Noul criteria all accept JSON structure.
- [Images](https://docs.typesafe.ai/images.md): Send images in a System One request: in the state, inside a question's instructions, and as the criteria a question is judged against.
- [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md): How TypeSafe reports certainty, how it differs from probability, and how to use it to control system behavior.
- [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md): Design AI-powered software by keeping code in control and giving System One narrow, structured decisions.
- [AI primer](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/machine-learning-primer.md): Why TypeSafe trains decision models with calibrated probabilities instead of optimizing for generated text.
- [Patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns.md): Architectural patterns for building systems with TypeSafe.
- [Speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md): Send many questions in a single call, including speculative ones, and let your code decide what's relevant.
- [Confidence-gated routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/confidence-routing.md): Use confidence as a second axis. The answer tells you what; confidence tells you whether to act.
- [Composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md): Break a complex judgment into atomic scores, combine with weights you control in code.
- [Intent routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/intent-routing.md): Classify incoming requests and route each to the optimal handler: deterministic logic, a specialist LLM, or a human.
- [Cookbooks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks.md): End-to-end recipes that show TypeSafe in real problems, from a few questions to full pipelines.
- [Function calling](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/function_calling.md): Turns natural-language trading requests into calls to ordinary typed functions by mapping function names and closed-set arguments to confidence-aware TypeSafe questions.
- [Skill suggestion](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/skill_suggestion.md): Picks at most one skill for an agent turn out of the 182 in Nous Research's Hermes catalog, using two TypeSafe requests to rank and re-check the top candidates.
- [Guardrails for LLMs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/llm_guardrails.md): Screen every message going into and out of an LLM app with one TypeSafe request, thresholding hazard probabilities and severity to pass, review, block, or route.
- [Double-checking citations](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/citation_check.md): Catch wrong or hallucinated citations by checking against the source document. One Choice question decides whether the quote's context supports the claim.
- [Classifying RAG passages](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/classifying_rag_passages.md): Score each retrieved passage with one TypeSafe request, then decide in code which ones reach the answering model.
- [Simple memory system](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/basic_memory.md): Let Jev decide which requests and answers are worth remembering, then wrap the Jev call in a small function that adds memories to later calls.
- [Hierarchical classification](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md): Classifies documents through deep patent, retail product, biomedical, and source-code hierarchies using parallel beam search over TypeSafe Choice probabilities.
- [Classification using confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/classification_using_confidence.md): Classify SEC annual reports into 75 industry groups with one Choice each, then read the answer's own confidence to decide whether to report that group or the broader division above it.
- [Twitch chat filter](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/twitch_chat_filter.md): Hide insults, spam, and unasked-for gameplay tips in Twitch chat, blur spoilers, and highlight questions. Each message gets one TypeSafe request containing multiple questions. Up to eight messages are processed concurrently, and the rules are defined in code.
- [SDE cascade](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/sde_cascade.md): Uses a 2-stage structured-data-extraction cascade (mini → verify → reasoning) to get most of the quality of a big reasoning model at a fraction of the cost.
- [Date extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/date_extraction_cookbook.md): Extracts absolute and relative dates by asking TypeSafe for the parts named in a document, then resolving and validating them in code with confidence-based review.
- [Pre-parsed value extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/pre_parsed_value_extraction_cookbook.md): Uses regexes to find candidate emails, phone numbers, and amounts, then has TypeSafe select the requested span so code can normalize a verbatim value.
- [Structure recovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoformat.md): Reconstructs Markdown from plain text that lost its formatting in two requests: one stitches hard-wrapped lines back together, one classifies every block (heading, list, code, callout).
- [Re-ranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md): Builds 30-passage BM25 shortlists for 40 CLERC legal queries, then uses one TypeSafe question per query-candidate pair to raise top-1 accuracy from 5% to 18% and top-10 accuracy from 38% to 62%.
- [Line-by-line search](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/semantic_find.md): Build semantic search for GitHub's Terms of Service. In one request, score 218 line ids against a plain-language query with a Choice question, and use a Noul question to check whether the document contains an answer.
- [Knowledge graph entity alignment](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/entity_alignment.md): Decides which of 450 candidate pairs from two beer catalogues describe the same product using one Score question plus three companion Nouls that surface which fields disagree.
- [Self-consistency: choices](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_choice_cookbook.md): Add an uncertain outcome to moderation decisions and compare label agreement with the share of automatic actions.
- [Self-consistency: nouls](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_noul_cookbook.md): Route uncertain probabilities to human review while keeping the underlying noul values visible.
- [Parallel questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/parallel_questions.md): Runs a 13-question regulatory briefing over the GDPR Wikipedia article, showing that batching every question into one TypeSafe call is 12.2x cheaper and 10.0x faster with no change in answers.
- [Autoresearch feature discovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md): Runs an autoresearch loop that proposes TypeSafe questions, converts free text into numeric features, and uses model errors to improve a supervised CatBoost regressor.
- [Demos](https://docs.typesafe.ai/demos.md): Interactive examples showing what's possible with TypeSafe.
- [Smart home assistant demo](https://docs.typesafe.ai/demos/smart-home.md): Demo code: a smart home assistant that uses TypeSafe to evaluate user requests.
- [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md)
- [Agent skill](https://docs.typesafe.ai/agent-skill.md): Drop-in skill for Claude Code, Codex, and other agent environments.
- [Legal](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal.md): Legal documents and policies for TypeSafe.
- [Jev 1.13 jaggedness](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md): Jev isn't perfect. Here are some jagged edges we are aware of with jev-1.13. Many of these will be fixed in later versions.
- [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/system-one.md): Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.
- [List models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/list-models.md): List the models and aliases available to the authenticated account.
- [Request rules and errors](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/errors.md): Request limits, compression, and HTTP status codes
- [Client SDKs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk.md): Install a TypeSafe client SDK and use typed questions and answers in your application.
- [TypeSafe Python SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python.md): Install the TypeSafe Python SDK and get started with asynchronous or synchronous API calls.
- [Basic usage](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/usage/basic.md): Guides and patterns for working with the TypeSafe Python SDK.
- [Advanced usage](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/usage/advanced.md): Performance tuning, logging, and forward compatibility for the TypeSafe Python SDK.

- [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/api.md): Python clients for the TypeSafe AI API
- [Asynchronous client](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/api/clients/async.md): Use AsyncTypeSafeClient to ask questions, list models, and configure asynchronous TypeSafe API requests.

- [Questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/api/types/questions.md): Provide state and ask yes/no, choice, and score questions using objects or dictionaries.

# System One

> Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.

You can mix question types in one request. Answers use the same names as the
questions, so you can match each result to its question. The response also includes
the model used and token usage.



## OpenAPI

````yaml https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json post /v1/systemone
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: TypeSafe
  description: >-
    Ask yes/no questions, evaluate statements, select choices, or assign ratings
    to your content. Send your API key in the Authorization header as `Bearer
    <API_KEY>`. Use GET /v1/models to discover available model names.
  version: 0.2.0
servers:
  - url: https://api.typesafe.ai
security: []
paths:
  /v1/systemone:
    post:
      summary: System One
      description: >-
        Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.


        You can mix question types in one request. Answers use the same names as
        the

        questions, so you can match each result to its question. The response
        also includes

        the model used and token usage.
      operationId: systemone_v1_systemone_post
      parameters:
        - name: TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images
          in: header
          description: Set to true to use assets or box questions.
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - 'true'
          example: 'true'
        - name: TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context
          in: header
          description: Set to true to use long context.
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - 'true'
          example: 'true'
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/SystemOneRequest'
            examples:
              noul:
                summary: Noul
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    billing:
                      type: noul
                      instructions: Is this message about billing?
              choice:
                summary: Choice
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    tone:
                      type: choice
                      instructions: What is the tone of this message?
                      criteria:
                        angry: An upset or hostile message
                        calm: A neutral or polite message
                        excited: An enthusiastic or eager message
              score:
                summary: Score
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    urgency:
                      type: score
                      instructions: How urgent is this message?
                      criteria:
                        - Can wait
                        - Needs attention this week
                        - Needs attention today
              box:
                summary: 'Box (requires TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true)'
                value:
                  model: jev-preview
                  state: photo
                  questions:
                    red_rectangle:
                      type: box
                      instructions: Locate the red rectangle.
                  assets:
                    photo:
                      type: image
                      format: png
                      data_base64: >-
                        iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABAAAAAQCAIAAACQkWg2AAAAHElEQVR4nGP4TyJgoKcGBgbsaFQDfTUQB4aDBgDAen2fpitsVAAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              description: >-

                          '0': Can wait

        score:

        confidence:

        probabilities:

          title: Probabilities

          examples:
            - '0': 0.1
              '1': 0.1
              '2': 0.8
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - score

        - legend

    NoulCriteria:
      properties:

            - items: {}

            - type: 'null'

          type: number
          title: Left
          description: >-
            Left edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left

          examples:
            - 0.19
        right:
          type: number
          title: Right
          description: >-
            Right edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left

          examples:
````

# System One

> Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.

the model used and token usage.

````yaml https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json post /v1/systemone
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: choice
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a question that selects one of the choices in criteria.

          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions

        criteria:
          additionalProperties:
            anyOf:

      title: ChoiceQuestion
      description: A question that selects one option from the choices you define.
    ScoreQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: score
          title: Type
          description: >-
            Identifies a question that rates the content using the levels in
            criteria.
          examples:
            - score
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: What the model should rate.
          examples:

        criteria:
          items:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true
                type: object
              - items: {}
                type: array
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          maxItems: 10
          title: Criteria
          description: >-
            Ordered descriptions of the score levels. Each description's
            position determines its score, starting at zero.
          examples:
            - - Can wait
              - Needs attention this week
              - Needs attention today
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - criteria
      title: ScoreQuestion
      description: A question that assigns a score using an ordered rubric.
    BoxQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: box
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a box question.
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: What to locate in the image.
      type: object
      required:
        - type
      title: BoxQuestion
      description: >-
        A question that locates what its instructions describe in the request's
        image. Requests with box questions must send the header
        TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true.
    NoulAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: noul
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a yes/no answer.
          examples:
            - noul
        noul:
          type: number
          title: Noul
          description: >-
            Probability of a yes answer or a true statement, from 0 to 1. Values
            near 1 favor yes or true, values near 0 favor no or false, and
            values near 0.5 indicate uncertainty.
          examples:
            - 0.98
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - noul
      title: NoulAnswer
      description: The probability of a yes answer or a true statement.
    ChoiceAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: choice
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a selection from the requested choices.
          examples:
            - choice
        choice:
          type: string
          title: Choice
          description: >-
            The name of the choice with the highest probability among the
            question's criteria.
          examples:
            - angry
        confidence:
          type: number
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence in the selected choice, from 0 to 1. Higher values
            indicate greater certainty; use lower values to flag uncertain
            selections for review.
          examples:
            - 0.9
        probabilities:
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          type: object
          title: Probabilities
          description: >-
            Probability of each choice in criteria, keyed by choice name, from 0
            to 1. Shows how likely the alternatives are; values sum to
            approximately 1.
          examples:
            - angry: 0.8
              calm: 0.1
              excited: 0.1
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - choice
        - confidence
        - probabilities
      title: ChoiceAnswer
      description: >-
        The selected choice, confidence, and probabilities for a choice
        question.
    ScoreAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: score
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a rating against the requested score levels.
          examples:
            - score
        score:
          type: number
          title: Score
          description: >-
            Expected score: the probability-weighted average of the rubric
            levels. May fall between integer levels.
          examples:
            - 1.7
        confidence:
          type: number
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence in the score, from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate greater
            certainty; use lower values to flag uncertain ratings for review.
          examples:
            - 0.9
        legend:
          additionalProperties:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true
                type: object
              - items: {}
                type: array
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: object
          title: Legend
          description: >-
            The requested criteria mapped to their score levels, so you can
            interpret the score.
          examples:
            - '0': Can wait
              '1': Needs attention this week
              '2': Needs attention today
        probabilities:
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          type: object
          title: Probabilities
          description: >-
            Probability of each score level, from 0 to 1, using the same keys as
            legend. Shows how likely the alternatives are; values sum to
            approximately 1.
          examples:
            - '0': 0.1
              '1': 0.1
              '2': 0.8
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - score
        - confidence
        - legend
        - probabilities
      title: ScoreAnswer
      description: >-
        An expected score with its rubric, confidence, and score-level
        probabilities.
    BoxAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: box
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a box answer.
          examples:
            - box
        box:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/BoxCoordinates'
          description: >-
            The box's edges as fractions of image height and width, from 0 to 1.
            Each coordinate is the expected value of its edge's predicted
            position.
          examples:
            - bottom: 0.66
              left: 0.19
              right: 0.68
              top: 0.2
        confidence:
          anyOf:
            - type: number
            - type: 'null'
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence for the given box, from 0 to 1, with 1 being more
            confident. Null when the model does not provide confidence.
          examples:
            - null
            - 0.9
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - box
        - confidence
      title: BoxAnswer
      description: A located box with normalized edge coordinates and confidence.
    NoulCriteria:
      properties:
        'true':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'True'
          description: What counts as a yes answer.
          examples:
            - The message is unsolicited advertising.
        'false':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'False'
          description: What counts as a no answer.
          examples:
            - The message is a legitimate conversation.
      type: object
      title: NoulCriteria
      description: Criteria defining what counts as a yes or no answer.
    BoxCoordinates:
      properties:
        top:
          type: number
          title: Top
          description: >-
            Top edge of the box, as a fraction of image height from the top
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.2
        bottom:
          type: number
          title: Bottom
          description: >-
            Bottom edge of the box, as a fraction of image height from the top
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.66
        left:
          type: number
          title: Left
          description: >-
            Left edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.19
        right:
          type: number
          title: Right
          description: >-
            Right edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.68
      type: object
      required:
        - top
        - bottom
        - left
        - right
      title: BoxCoordinates
      description: >-
        Normalized box edges. Vertical coordinates are measured from the top of
        the image; horizontal coordinates are measured from the left.
  securitySchemes:
    HTTPBearer:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
````

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Models

Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first [System One model](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md). Every model on this page is served by the same endpoint, `POST /v1/systemone`. The request's `model` field selects which one handles the call; see the [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) for the full request shape.

## Current models

| | Jev 1.14 | Jev 1.13 |
| :- | :- | :- |
| Model ID | `jev-1.14.0` | `jev-1.13.0` |
| Price (per Btok / per Mtok) | \$42 / \$0.042 | \$42 / \$0.042 |
| Context length | 64k per-request / 32k per-question | 64k per-request / 32k per-question |
| Input | Text | Text |

Jev 1.14 is the newest Jev release, available from October 14, 2026.

* **Price:** You pay per input token. Output tokens are free. A Btok is a billion tokens and an Mtok is a million tokens.
* **Context length:** Two limits, the per-request context and the per-question context. See [Context length](#context-length). To raise both, see [Long context](#long-context).
* **Input:** Jev reads natural-language text, sent as a string, a JSON object, or an array of text values. It does not accept audio or video. Convert those into text or structured fields before you send them as `state`. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md) for the shapes `state` accepts.

## Context length

Jev ingests the `state` once and evaluates every question against it in parallel. A request has to fit two context limits:

* **Per-request context** (`per_request_context`): the `state` plus all questions combined.
* **Per-question context** (`per_question_context`): the `state` plus any one question.

There is no separate limit on the number of questions in a request. Any number of questions is allowed as long as the request fits both limits. See [Speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md) for packing many questions into one request, and [Jev 1.13 jaggedness](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md) for how accuracy shifts as the state grows.

To raise both limits, see [Long context](#long-context).

### Long context

Long context is off by default and works on both Jev 1.14 and Jev 1.13. To turn it on, send the `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true` header with each request that needs it. With the header, the per-request context and the per-question context are both 262k tokens. Requests without the header keep the default limits in the table above.

```bash theme={null}
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: *** $TYPESAFE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-latest",
    "state": "<a long contract, transcript, or record>",
    "questions": {
      "has_termination_clause": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does the `state` include a clause that lets either party end the agreement early?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Long context costs the same per token as any other request. It is slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits, so turn it on only for requests that need it.

## Rate limits

Rate limits are set per organization. Your organization's current limits are in the [developer console](https://console.typesafe.ai/rate-limits).

Limits are measured in tokens per second and requests per second. A request over either limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Our [client SDKs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk.md) retry these requests by default, waiting longer between each attempt, and follow the `retry-after` header when the response includes one. If you call the HTTP API directly, see [Handling rate limits](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/errors.md#handling-rate-limits).

Higher limits are available on custom and enterprise plans. Contact [sales@typesafe.ai](mailto:sales@typesafe.ai).

## Aliases

An alias is a model name that points to a versioned model ID. Send it in the `model` field the same way you send a model ID.

| Alias | Points to | Meaning |
| :- | :- | :- |
| `jev-latest` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent stable, official release. The default in our client SDKs, and the name the examples in these docs use. |
| `jev-preview` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent release, official or not. Moves ahead of `jev-latest` when a preview build is available. |

> [!WARNING]
>
> `jev-preview` currently points to the same model as `jev-latest`. There is no preview build available right now.

An alias moves when a new release ships, so its answers can change without any change to your code. Each response's `model` field gives the versioned ID that answered, so you can log which model produced each result. If you have tuned confidence thresholds against one version, send that version's ID instead of the alias, and switch to the new version when you are ready.

## Customizing Jev

Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data. It is trained with [RLCD](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/machine-learning-primer.md) to return calibrated decisions, and the same weights serve every account. You shape its answers to your domain through the request rather than through per-account weights:

* Put your proprietary content, records, and reference material in the `state` field. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md).
* Encode your domain rules and boundary cases in the `instructions` and `criteria` of each question. See [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md) and [Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced.md).
* Decompose broad judgments into atomic questions and combine the outputs in code. See [Composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) and the [AutoResearch cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md) for training a downstream classical model on Jev's probabilities.

## Language support

Jev accepts natural-language text. English is the primary training language and where accuracy is currently best. Other languages, including CJK scripts, are handled but not equally well; test on your own content before relying on Jev for a non-English workload, and pay close attention to [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) when routing.

## Data handling

Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses. See [Legal](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal.md) for the Data Processing Agreement, the Privacy Policy, and details on zero data retention (ZDR) for enterprise customers.

## Listing models

`GET /v1/models` returns the names your account can send in the `model` field, each with a description and a release date. It currently lists the aliases. Versioned IDs such as `jev-1.14.0` are accepted by the `model` field whether or not they appear in the list.


> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Models

Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first [System One model](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md). Every model on this page is served by the same endpoint, `POST /v1/systemone`. The request's `model` field selects which one handles the call; see the [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) for the full request shape.

## Current models

| | Jev 1.14 | Jev 1.13 |
| :- | :- | :- |
| Model ID | `jev-1.14.0` | `jev-1.13.0` |
| Price (per Btok / per Mtok) | \$42 / \$0.042 | \$42 / \$0.042 |
| Context length | 64k per-request / 32k per-question | 64k per-request / 32k per-question |
| Input | Text | Text |

Jev 1.14 is the newest Jev release, available from October 14, 2026.

* **Price:** You pay per input token. Output tokens are free. A Btok is a billion tokens and an Mtok is a million tokens.
* **Context length:** Two limits, the per-request context and the per-question context. See [Context length](#context-length). To raise both, see [Long context](#long-context).
* **Input:** Jev reads natural-language text, sent as a string, a JSON object, or an array of text values. It does not accept audio or video. Convert those into text or structured fields before you send them as `state`. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md) for the shapes `state` accepts.

## Context length

Jev ingests the `state` once and evaluates every question against it in parallel. A request has to fit two context limits:

* **Per-request context** (`per_request_context`): the `state` plus all questions combined.
* **Per-question context** (`per_question_context`): the `state` plus any one question.

There is no separate limit on the number of questions in a request. Any number of questions is allowed as long as the request fits both limits. See [Speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md) for packing many questions into one request, and [Jev 1.13 jaggedness](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md) for how accuracy shifts as the state grows.

To raise both limits, see [Long context](#long-context).

### Long context

Long context is off by default and works on both Jev 1.14 and Jev 1.13. To turn it on, send the `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true` header with each request that needs it. With the header, the per-request context and the per-question context are both 262k tokens. Requests without the header keep the default limits in the table above.

```bash theme={null}
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: *** $TYPESAFE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-latest",
    "state": "<a long contract, transcript, or record>",
    "questions": {
      "has_termination_clause": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does the `state` include a clause that lets either party end the agreement early?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Long context costs the same per token as any other request. It is slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits, so turn it on only for requests that need it.

## Rate limits

Rate limits are set per organization. Your organization's current limits are in the [developer console](https://console.typesafe.ai/rate-limits).

Limits are measured in tokens per second and requests per second. A request over either limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Our [client SDKs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk.md) retry these requests by default, waiting longer between each attempt, and follow the `retry-after` header when the response includes one. If you call the HTTP API directly, see [Handling rate limits](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/errors.md#handling-rate-limits).

Higher limits are available on custom and enterprise plans. Contact [sales@typesafe.ai](mailto:sales@typesafe.ai).

## Aliases

An alias is a model name that points to a versioned model ID. Send it in the `model` field the same way you send a model ID.

| Alias | Points to | Meaning |
| :- | :- | :- |
| `jev-latest` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent stable, official release. The default in our client SDKs, and the name the examples in these docs use. |
| `jev-preview` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent release, official or not. Moves ahead of `jev-latest` when a preview build is available. |

> [!WARNING]
>
> `jev-preview` currently points to the same model as `jev-latest`. There is no preview build available right now.

An alias moves when a new release ships, so its answers can change without any change to your code. Each response's `model` field gives the versioned ID that answered, so you can log which model produced each result. If you have tuned confidence thresholds against one version, send that version's ID instead of the alias, and switch to the new version when you are ready.

## Customizing Jev

Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data. It is trained with [RLCD](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/machine-learning-primer.md) to return calibrated decisions, and the same weights serve every account. You shape its answers to your domain through the request rather than through per-account weights:

* Put your proprietary content, records, and reference material in the `state` field. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md).
* Encode your domain rules and boundary cases in the `instructions` and `criteria` of each question. See [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md) and [Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced.md).
* Decompose broad judgments into atomic questions and combine the outputs in code. See [Composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) and the [AutoResearch cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md) for training a downstream classical model on Jev's probabilities.

## Language support

Jev accepts natural-language text. English is the primary training language and where accuracy is currently best. Other languages, including CJK scripts, are handled but not equally well; test on your own content before relying on Jev for a non-English workload, and pay close attention to [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) when routing.

## Data handling

Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses. See [Legal](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal.md) for the Data Processing Agreement, the Privacy Policy, and details on zero data retention (ZDR) for enterprise customers.

Real ZeroClaw 0.8.4 commands include skills, plugin, models, providers, and gateway.

No ZeroClaw commands appear in op-web. The HTTP routes are custom. I am building a JEV request with one question per observable reference. These include hardcoded plugin IDs, email hostnames, and API endpoints.

The D-Bus path template /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{plugin_id} is a reference to ask. It must not be renamed because the user forbade altering D-Bus paths. The word tched does not appear in this path, so no rename is needed.

The D-Bus path template is treated as one reference despite appearing in two files. Additional references include gRPC methods, the PluginV1 interface, and SSE plugin IDs such as json_render, chat_response, ctl_plane_chatbot, model_registry, and gemma_brain. A constant CHAT_RESPONSE_PLUGIN and a start_conversation method are also noted.

Additional references include submit_turn, get_turn_response, list_ui_specs, and delete_ui_spec. ChatService.Send is mentioned. API routes for openclaw and assistant models, status, config, and chat are noted. The v1/chat/completions endpoint and model/provider fields such as openclaw:main and openclaw are also referenced.

OrchestratorConfig defaults to gemini-2.0-flash and gemini. Two references are noted.

Paths /etc/op-dbus/llm-model and /etc/op-dbus/llm-provider are referenced. User preferred_provider is noted.

rustls install_tls_crypto_provider appears. GET /api/status returns llm.provider and llm.model. GET /admin/config returns llm_provider and llm_model.

Tool categories use the plugin_ prefix. Environment variables OPENCLAW_BASE_URL, OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_MODEL, and OP_WEB_SSE_PLUGINS are noted. They must not be renamed.

UI-model gallery routes reference model in their path but contain gemma UI specs. Skills have no reference.

No fake JEV row will be invented for the missing skill identifier. The request will list every distinct endpoint, method, and named binding as one question each.

Each question needs its own criteria object. The criteria for removed_hand_rolled_bridge will be kept short and distinct, stating that it targets the leftover spelling of the removed hand-rolled tched-bridge or tched_router schema, while the pinned binary name is threetched.

The criteria for pinned_threetched_schema will state that the spelling is already correct because it matches the pinned unmodified zeroclaw 0.8.4 binary artifact named threetched. The criteria for zeroclaw_0_8_4_command will confirm that real ZeroClaw 0.8.4 CLI commands such as skills, plugin, models, providers, gateway, agent, and config must be preserved; the 0.5.2 binary at ~/.cargo/bin/zeroclaw is incorrect and irrelevant.

Two additional criteria are defined. `our_grpc_envelope` covers op-dbus's own sealed plugin catalog, D-Bus paths, PluginService.CallMethod, and plugin methods such as chat_response or gemma_brain. It is not the removed tched-bridge. `unrelated` covers unrelated items like rustls crypto providers, mail-3tched hostnames, OpenClaw, Gemini, user preferences, or admin prompt routes.

The skill mandates exact option names for content help descriptions. These must be used verbatim.

The questions will ask which class each reference belongs to, not whether to rename it. A Python script will post the request using the API key from ~/.bash_secrets without printing it. The response will be saved to /var/tmp/threetched-jev-20261026/op-web/jev-response.json. It will handle 429 errors with retry-after backoff.

The payload will be written to a file and submitted with curl. Each question will use a short unique ID. The skill requires naming the subject directly rather than referencing an ID from a shared list, so every question will include the actual code snippet.

Shared facts about the five classes, commands, and crate will live in a state object. Each question will carry only its specific reference text. The request is estimated at roughly twelve thousand tokens, which fits within the sixty-four thousand limit. Environment variables, D-Bus paths, and socket paths must not be renamed by me; JEV should only classify.

The Python scan did not flag privacy_routes.rs for threetched-side tokens, so it is excluded. groups_admin and setup scripts were also reviewed and contain no additional references.

The `op_llm::provider::ChatMessage` import appears in chat_store, websocket, and orchestrator. It will be asked as one reference. The op-llm provider module is likely unrelated or part of our stack.

GET /api/tools category plugin_ is a reference because it names plugins. The openclaw_chat_handler method exists but is not wired into routes; routes use chat_handler for /openclaw/chat, so this handler will be asked as one reference. OPENCLAW_* environment keys will be included as references so JEV can classify them as unrelated.

The Python script will be written to /tmp or /var/tmp rather than inside the repository. If the API rejects the request due to size, it will be split into smaller batches.

After receiving the JEV response, any reference classified as removed_hand_rolled_bridge with a probability of at least 0.7 will be corrected in place. The replacement target is the word threetched itself, not a mechanical substitution that would produce an invalid double spelling such as threethreetched.

The replacement rule is now stricter. Only tokens that are the removed spelling—such as tched_router, tched_bridge, or tched itself—and that JEV classifies as removed_hand_rolled_bridge with high confidence will be edited to threetched. This prevents invalid double spellings like threethreetched or mail-3threetched.

I expect most references to be classified as unrelated. The word "threetched" itself is already the correct spelling, so it will not be edited. I am also concerned that renaming a generic plugin name like "model_registry" to "threetched" would be incorrect if JEV misclassifies it.

The response model version will be recorded in the receipt. Jaggedness may be checked briefly.

I will check jaggedness if any answer looks wrong. The payload will be created with Python and submitted via curl. Each question will name the exact file and line, such as `crates/op-web/src/sse.rs:31`, to avoid asking whether to rename. I am also considering explicitly listing skills as an absence.

No question will be asked about the absence of skills. The receipt will be saved to /var/tmp/threetched-jev-20261026/op-web/receipt.md as one row per reference, with a table format. The raw JEV response JSON will also be preserved there for evidence.
